reason: Part a is an arithmetic sum that can be seen as an area under the line of terms, with the term count made visible by a slider. Part b is left without a scene.

scenes.title: Counting the terms from r = 15 to r = 48
scenes.purpose: See each term as a unit-wide strip under the line y = 5r - 2, so the number of terms is 34 and the total is 5287.

elements.value: Last term at $r = {k}$: $5r - 2 = {5*k-2}$. Number of terms $= {k} - 15 + 1 = {k-14}$. Sum so far $= {area(R)}$

steps.text: Each strip is one term of $\sum (5r-2)$, centred on an integer $r$. The first strip is at $r=15$, height $a = 5(15)-2 = 73$. The line rises by $d = 5$ per step, so the series is arithmetic. This is the first M1.

Drag $k$ to $16$: the strips at $r=15$ and $r=16$ give $2$ terms, which is $16-15+1$, not $16-15$. Both ends count. Now drag $k$ to $48$ and the count reads $n = 48 - 15 + 1 = 34$. This is the M1 for the number of terms.
At $k=48$ the last term is $l = 5(48)-2 = 238$. Use $l = a + (n-1)d = 73 + 33\times 5$, not $a + nd$. Then $S = \frac{34}{2}(73+238) = 17\times 311$. This is the third M1.
The shaded area equals the sum because the strips average out the slope of the line: the area reads $5287$. This is the A1. Drag $Q$ along the line to see that the heights go up in steps of $5$.

guide.what_you_see: The line $y=5r-2$ with unit-wide strips under it, one for each term of $\sum (5r-2)$, each centred on a whole number $r$. The shaded strips start at $r=15$ and end at the slider value $k$, so the shaded area is the sum of the terms so far.

legend.meaning: The line $y=5r-2$, whose height at each whole number $r$ is the term $5r-2$ of the series. Here $r$ is drawn along the horizontal axis.
The point $(15, 73)$, the first term of the series, so $a=73$.
The point $(48, 238)$, the last term of the series, so $l=238$.
The shaded strips from $r=14.5$ to $r=k+0.5$. Each strip has width $1$ and height $5r-2$, so its area is one term, and the total area is the sum of the terms from $r=15$ to $r=k$.
The vertical line at $r=k+0.5$ that marks the right-hand edge of the last strip.
A point you can drag along the line $y=5r-2$ to read off the term heights.

interact.do: Drag the slider between $15$ and $48$. Try $16$ first, then move it up to $48$.
interact.watch: At $k=16$ there are two strips, which is $16-15+1$. As you drag, the strip count is $k-14$. At $k=48$ there are $34$ strips, the last height is $238$, and the shaded area is $5287$. At the starting value $k=30$ there are $16$ terms and the sum is $1768$.

interact.do: Drag $Q$ along the line, moving it from one whole-number $r$ to the next.
interact.watch: The height goes up by exactly $5$ for each step of $1$ in $r$. This constant difference is what makes the series arithmetic with $d=5$.

question_link.text: The strips are the terms of $\sum_{r=15}^{48}(5r-2)$. $A$ gives the first term $a=73$ and the constant rise of $5$ gives $d=5$ (first M1). The strip count $48-15+1=34$ is the second M1. $B$ gives $l=238$, which feeds $\frac{34}{2}(73+238)$ (third M1), and the full shaded area $5287$ is the A1.
